title: SSO attribute intersection grants unintended admin privileges
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A production customer reported that users in a particular SAML group mapping gained admin-level UI controls intermittently after a role-mapping change. The incident surfaced as a customer escalation (CS-99821) and we reproduced an edge case where overlapping SSO attributes (legacy 'admin_group' + new team-scoped 'team:platform:admins') led to an intersection rule erroneously resolving to a superset role. This ticket tracks the triage, fix, audit-log improvements, QA, and rollout for the patch and follow-ups (migration + monitoring).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure SAML IdP with two attributes: 'groups' containing legacy 'admin_group' and a new attribute 'team:platform:admins'.
2) Redwood SSO mapping configured with both a legacy-role rule (map 'admin_group' -> role:organization-admin) and a scoped rule (map 'team:platform:admins' -> role:team-admin).
3) Simulate IdP assertion that includes both attributes via test SAML assertion payload (see test fixture test-fixtures/saml/intersection-assertion.xml).
4) Authenticate as a user and observe UI; the account intermittently shows organization-admin controls (billing/organization settings) due to mapping precedence fallback.
root_cause: RBAC v2 mapping engine merges attribute-derived roles using a set-union followed by precedence heuristics. A recent change introduced an 'intersection-optimistic' path that attempted to collapse compound mappings for backward compatibility; when legacy and scoped mappings coexist the collapse sometimes resolved to the broader legacy role. Audit events were emitted but lacked the full attribute context (only role outcome was recorded), making fast triage difficult.
fix_summary: 1) Rework mapping resolution to use deterministic precedence: explicit scoped mappings take precedence over legacy group mappings unless an override is explicitly configured. 2) Patch mapping engine to record full assertion attributes and intermediate resolution steps into audit log entries. 3) Add a migration script to re-evaluate existing org mappings and flag configurations that rely on legacy/scoped overlap. 4) Emergency API validation preventing assignment of organization-admin by inheritance during the hotfix window.
rollout_plan: Canary deploy patch to 10% of auth traffic in hosted regions (region-us-west-2) and 1 Dedicated customer for validation.
Keep previous mapping engine binary as guarded fallback with feature flag 'rbac_v2_safe_mode' for immediate rollback.
After 48 hours with no regressions, expand to 50% -> 100% and run migration job for flagged orgs during off-peak hours.
Notify affected customers and update release notes with mitigation steps and audit log access instructions.
qa_plan: Unit tests covering precedence matrix between legacy, scoped, and override rules (new table-driven tests).
Integration test that replays real customer SAML assertions (redacted) and verifies role outcomes across mapping permutations.
E2E smoke in canary for UI controls visibility and CLI token scopes; automated check validates no user gains org-admin unless explicit mapping present.
Pen-test/privilege-review with Security to validate no lateral escalation paths remain.
